messages:
alice (DevEx): heads up — hitting SSL verification failures in our quickstart on Windows with python 3.8/3.9. sample app using requests/httpx/aiohttp fails with SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed

ben (Windows QA): seen this locally too. usually on machines behind corp proxy, but also repros on a clean 3.8 venv on my windows vm.

alice (DevEx): minimal repro (3.8.10, venv):
```python
import requests
requests.get('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings')
```
-> SSLError on first TLS handshake, full trace points to _ssl.c:...

carmen (Python SDK): thanks. can you paste output of `python -m certifi` and `pip show urllib3 httpx requests`? also which redwood-python version?

alice (DevEx): certifi: C:\venv\Lib\site-packages\certifi\cacert.pem
redwood-python==0.3.6
requests 2.31.0
httpx 0.25.0
urllib3 2.0.4

carmen (Python SDK): ok. likely the issue is our transport falling back to platform SSLContext which on windows+older CPython/openSSL build doesn't automatically pick up certifi bundle. workaround: set env var `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` to certifi.where(), or for aiohttp/httpx create SSLContext with `cafile=certifi.where()`

ben (Windows QA): confirmed workaround: `set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=C:\venv\Lib\site-packages\certifi\cacert.pem` and restart venv -> requests works. for aiohttp i did `ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())` in the sample.

dave (Eng): also flagging a separate but related problem: Python 3.8 on Windows defaults can cause weird asyncio behavior when mixing threads. sample async quickstart uses `asyncio.run()` inside a thread in one example — on 3.8 that can blow up without explicit policy. might be confusing for Windows devs.

alice (DevEx): this is high friction for onboarding — Windows is a big chunk of our early adopters. can we include a fix + docs?

carmen (Python SDK): yes. plan: (1) change SDK transport to explicitly use certifi.where() as the default CA file on Windows (when verify is not overridden), (2) add a short note in quickstart about `WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy` for 3.8 when mixing threads, (3) ship typed stubs for AsyncClient so IDEs show proper typing. i've got a draft PR and tests.

alice (DevEx): awesome. can we also add a tiny troubleshooting section to the windows sample that shows the env var/workaround? saves support tickets.

carmen (Python SDK): will do. PR draft: #898 (contains transport change + docs + tests). tagging ben for windows QA review.

ben (Windows QA): will smoke test across 3.8/3.9/3.10/3.12 on monday. any pref on backport to 0.3.6 patch?

carmen (Python SDK): plan to cut 0.3.7 with the cert fix + typing and patch the quickstart. if tests look green we can backport key change to 0.3.6-patch branch.

dave (Eng): tiny nit: include a small snippet to set policy in samples:
```python
import asyncio
import sys
if sys.platform == 'win32' and sys.version_info < (3,10):
    asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy())
```

alice (DevEx): perfect. once 0.3.7 is out i'll update the onboarding guide and add a short FAQ entry. thanks! :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: published redwood-python 0.3.7 to PyPI (tag: v0.3.7)

carmen (Python SDK): released. changelog includes: windows certifi default, async client types, quickstart eventloop note, tests. will follow up with the PR link and release notes.

alice (DevEx): closing the loop — huge help. pls ping when the backport PR exists so we can patch the pinned quickstarts in docs.
